# Section 05 — List mode (`-l` / `--list`), exact output formats

Binary: `/workspace/executable` = xz (XZ Utils) 5.8.2, liblzma 5.8.2.
All commands run with `LC_ALL=C`, cwd = `/tmp/xzprobe_list`. Raw captures: `/tmp/xztest/ref/list_*.out|.err`; exit-code record: `/tmp/xztest/ref/list_exitcodes.txt`.
Whitespace in this document was verified with `cat -A` / `sed -n l` and column indexing; `^I` notes below mean a literal TAB (0x09).

## Global notes (read first)

- **Program name in diagnostics**: error messages are prefixed with argv[0] as invoked, here `/workspace/executable: `. A clone invoked as `xz` must print `xz: `. Format: `PROG: FILENAME: MESSAGE` (or `PROG: MESSAGE` when no file is involved).
- **Exit codes observed in list mode**: `0` = success; `1` = any error (unrecognized format, corrupt/truncated data, empty file, missing file, stdin input). No warning/exit-2 case was found: trailing garbage after a valid stream is a hard *error* in list mode, not a warning.
- **`-q` / `-qq`**: `-q` does NOT suppress list-mode error messages. `-qq` suppresses the message but the exit code stays `1`. On valid files `-q`/`-qq` change nothing.
- **Machine dependence**: none observed in `-l` output. `MemUsage`/`Memory needed` reflects the filter chain's decoder memory requirement (here `--lzma2=dict=8MiB` -> 8454808 B), not host RAM (125.8 GiB) or core count (64). Files made with `-T0` on this 64-core machine still produced a single block for a 5 MiB input; the listing structure is identical to single-threaded files.
- All offsets/sizes in the `-lv`/`-lvv` tables and in robot mode are plain decimal byte counts. Only the `-l` table and the `-lv` summary use human-readable sizes.

xz -k --check=crc32  -c small.txt > check-crc32.xz       # 124 B
xz -k --check=crc64  -c small.txt > check-crc64.xz       # 128 B
xz -k --check=sha256 -c small.txt > check-sha256.xz      # 152 B
cat one.xz one.xz > two-streams.xz                       # 256 B, 2 streams
xz -k --format=lzma -c small.txt > one.lzma              # 75 B (.lzma/alone format)

Structure of `-lv`/`-lvv` output:

- Line 1: `FILENAME (N/M)` — N = 1-based index of this file, M = total number of file arguments.
- Summary block: 2-space indent, label left-aligned and padded to 18 characters, one space, then the value (values start at 0-based col 21 unless the label exceeds 18 chars). Labels in order: `Streams:`, `Blocks:`, `Compressed size:`, `Uncompressed size:`, `Ratio:`, `Check:`, `Stream Padding:`.
- Summary sizes: human-readable; when the unit is not `B`, the exact byte count is appended as ` (N B)`, e.g. `5120.0 KiB (5242880 B)`. `1024 B` and `2048 B` are shown as plain `N B` (threshold: sizes < 10000 use `B`).
- `  Streams:` section, then `  Blocks:` section. The `Blocks:` section is omitted entirely when the file has 0 blocks (see `emptyinput.xz` below).
- `-lvv` adds three more summary lines after the Blocks section: `Memory needed:`, `Sizes in headers:` (`Yes`/`No`), `Minimum XZ Utils version:` (`5.0.0`).

Streams table (identical in `-lv` and `-lvv`), header literal:

```
    Stream    Blocks      CompOffset    UncompOffset        CompSize      UncompSize  Ratio  Check      Padding
```

Row format (deduced printf): `%10s %9s %15s %15s %15s %15s  %5s  %-10s %7s` — Stream (right, w10, cols 0-9), space, Blocks (right, w9), space, CompOffset (right, w15), space, UncompOffset (right, w15), space, CompSize (right, w15), space, UncompSize (right, w15), 2 spaces, Ratio (right, w5), 2 spaces, Check (left, w10), space, Padding (right, w7). All offsets/sizes plain decimal bytes.

Blocks table in `-lv`, header literal (same widths through Check, row format `%10s %9s %15s %15s %15s %15s  %5s  %s`):

```
    Stream     Block      CompOffset    UncompOffset       TotalSize      UncompSize  Ratio  Check
```

Blocks table in `-lvv`, header literal (CRC64 file; the CheckVal column width adapts, see §7):

```
    Stream     Block      CompOffset    UncompOffset       TotalSize      UncompSize  Ratio  Check      CheckVal          Header  Flags        CompSize    MemUsage  Filters
```

Extra `-lvv` columns after Check (left, w10) + space:

- `CheckVal` @ col 104: check value as lowercase hex, no separators; `---` for check=None. Left-aligned; field width = max(8, 2 x check size in bytes): 8 (None/CRC32), 16 (CRC64), 64 (SHA-256). Later columns shift accordingly (see §7 for exact anchors per check type).
- `Header`: block header size in bytes, right-aligned w6 after 2 spaces (`20` when sizes are stored, `12` otherwise).
- `Flags`: 2 chars after 2 spaces, left-aligned in a wide field; `cu` = block header contains compressed size (`c`) and uncompressed size (`u`); `--` = neither. Observed anchors: flags value at the column right after the Header field + 2 spaces.
- `CompSize`: compressed size of the block's data alone, right-aligned.
- `MemUsage`: decoder memory for this block, human-readable, rounded UP (`8454808 B` = 8.06 MiB shown as `9 MiB`).
- `Filters`: filter chain rendered as xz option strings, e.g. `--lzma2=dict=8MiB` (no space in `dict=8MiB`).

Observed 0-based token anchors for a CRC64 `-lvv` block row (value@end-col): Stream ends col 10, Block ends 20, CompOffset ends 36, UncompOffset ends 52, TotalSize ends 68, UncompSize ends 84, Ratio cols 86-90, Check @93, CheckVal @104 (16 chars), Header value ends col 128, Flags @130 (`cu`), CompSize ends col 151, MemUsage right-aligned ending col 163 (e.g. `   9 MiB`), Filters @165, left-aligned to end of line.

## 12. Ratio and size formatting rules

Ratio:

- `compressed / uncompressed` with `%.3f` (e.g. 128/1024 = `0.125`, 168/100 = `1.680`, 1208/5242880 = `0.000`).
- Rendered as `---` when uncompressed size is 0, and also when the ratio exceeds 9.999 (tiny.xz: 68/1 -> `---`; boundary inferred, not bisected). `---` is right-aligned in the width-5 field (`    ---` / `  ---`).

Human-readable sizes (observed with files of exact sizes 1023, 1024, 9999, 10000, 10239, 10240, 123456, 10485759, 10485760 bytes):

Command: `LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable -l sz1023.xz sz1024.xz sz9999.xz sz10000.xz sz10239.xz sz10240.xz sz123456.xz sz10485759.xz sz10485760.xz` — exit code **0**

stdout:
```
{{CAP:l_sizes.out}}
```
stderr: empty

Command: `LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable -lv sz10000.xz` — exit code **0** (excerpt lines 4-5):

```
{{CAP:lv_sz10000.out}}
```
stderr: empty

Rules (inferred from the boundaries above):

- size < 10000 B -> `N B` (so `1024 B`, `9999 B`; `0 B` for empty).
- 10000 <= size < 10240000 -> `X.Y KiB` with `%.1f` of size/1024 (10000 -> `9.8 KiB`; rounding can overflow the decade: 10239 -> `10.0 KiB`).
- 10240000 <= size < 10485760000 -> `X.Y MiB` of size/1048576 (10485759 -> `10.0 MiB`). Unit choice uses the raw byte value vs. `10000 * 1024^k` thresholds, made BEFORE rounding. Larger units (GiB, TiB) presumably continue the pattern (not probed — would need >10 GB files).
- In `-lv` summaries, when the unit is not `B`, the exact count is appended: `9.8 KiB (10000 B)`. In the `-l` table and in robot mode there are no parenthesized counts (robot is always plain bytes).

# Section 05 — List mode (`-l` / `--list`), exact output formats

Binary: `/workspace/executable` = xz (XZ Utils) 5.8.2, liblzma 5.8.2.

## Global notes (read first)

- **Program name in diagnostics**: error messages are prefixed with argv[0] as invoked, here `/workspace/executable: `. A clone invoked as `xz` must print `xz: `. Format: `PROG: FILENAME: MESSAGE` (or `PROG: MESSAGE` when no file is involved).
- **Exit codes observed in list mode**: `0` = success; `1` = any error (unrecognized format, corrupt/truncated data, empty file, missing file, stdin input). No warning/exit-2 case was found: trailing garbage after a valid stream is a hard *error* in list mode, not a warning.
- **`-q` / `-qq`**: `-q` does NOT suppress list-mode error messages. `-qq` suppresses the message but the exit code stays `1`. On valid files `-q`/`-qq` change nothing.
- **Machine dependence**: none observed in `-l` output. `MemUsage`/`Memory needed` reflects the filter chain's decoder memory requirement (here `--lzma2=dict=8MiB` -> 8454808 B), not host RAM (125.8 GiB) or core count (64). payload.resultSummary:
Assignment complete. Summary of what was delivered:

## Deliverables

- **Section file**: `/tmp/xztest/ref/sections/05_list.md` (1060 lines, ~45 KB). Generated programmatically from the raw captures (via `/tmp/xzprobe_list/gen.py` + `template.md`) so all stdout/stderr blocks are byte-verbatim, tabs included; `empty` is stated for empty streams. Verified: no unresolved placeholders, 92 fenced blocks, spot-checked against raw captures.
- **Raw captures**: 60 pairs of `/tmp/xztest/ref/list_<name>.out`/`.err`, all produced with `LC_ALL=C`; scratch dir `/tmp/xzprobe_list` holds test files and the `run.sh` capture harness.
- **Exit-code record**: `/tmp/xztest/ref/list_exitcodes.txt` (61 entries, command → exit code).

## Key findings (all in the md with verbatim evidence)

- **`-l` table**: header exactly `Strms  Blocks   Compressed Uncompressed  Ratio  Check   Filename` (64 chars); rows match `%5s %7s   %10s %12s  %5s  %-7s %s` (0-based column map documented). Multi-file totals: separator of exactly **79 dashes**, then a totals row with `N files` in the filename column.
- **`-lv`/`-lvv`**: `filename (N/M)` header; summary labels padded to 18 chars (values at col 21); Streams/Blocks tables with deduced printf formats and exact token anchors; `-lvv` adds CheckVal (lowercase hex, `---` for None; column width adapts: 8/8/16/64 for None/CRC32/CRC64/SHA-256, later columns shift), Header size, Flags (`cu`/`--`), CompSize, MemUsage (rounded **up**: 8454808 B → `9 MiB`), Filters (`--lzma2=dict=8MiB`), plus `Memory needed:`, `Sizes in headers: Yes/No`, `Minimum XZ Utils version: 5.0.0`. Multi-file runs end with a `Totals:` section after a blank line per file.
- **Robot mode**: TAB-separated records (`name`/`file`/`stream`/`block`/`summary`/`totals`), plain byte sizes, ratio `%.3f` or `---`, version `50000002`; full per-record field layouts documented. A zero `totals` line is emitted even on total failure (stdin/corrupt), with exit 1.
- **Formatting rules**: ratio `%.3f`, `---` when uncompressed=0 or ratio>9.999 (68.0 → `---`); sizes: `N B` below 10000 B, then `X.Y KiB` below 10240000 B, then MiB (thresholds on raw bytes before rounding — 10239 B → `10.0 KiB`, 10485759 B → `10.0 MiB`); `-lv` summaries append ` (N B)` when unit ≠ B.
- **Errors** (all exit 1, format `PROG: FILE: MSG` with argv[0] as prefix): `Too small to be a valid .xz file`, `File is empty`, `Compressed data is corrupt` (truncation AND trailing garbage — garbage is an error, not a warning; `-lvv` prints only the `name (1/1)` line first), `No such file or directory`, `File format not recognized` (.lzma is unsupported by `-l`), `--list does not support reading from standard input` (stdin refused entirely). `-q` does NOT suppress these; `-qq` suppresses the message but exit stays 1.

One caveat noted in the doc: the ratio `---` threshold (>9.999) and GiB/TiB unit continuation are inferred, not boundary-bisected (would have needed >10 GB test files).

"""Compare /workspace/src/filters.c against the reference binary."""
import subprocess, sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from oracle import ref_decode

FTEST = "/tmp/xztest/ftest"

def my_run(data, mode, filter_id=None, start=0, dist=None):
    if dist is not None:
        args = [FTEST, "delta", mode, str(dist)]
    else:
        args = [FTEST, "bcj", mode, "0x%X" % filter_id, str(start)]
    p = subprocess.run(args, input=data, capture_output=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError("ftest failed: %s" % p.stderr.decode())
    return p.stdout

def check_case(data, name, filter_id=None, start=0, dist=None, verbose=False):
    """Two-way differential check. Returns None on success, else a message."""
    kw = dict(filter_id=filter_id, start=start, dist=dist)
    # 1. my encode must be inverted by reference decode
    e = my_run(data, "enc", **kw)
    back = ref_decode(e, **kw)
    if back != data:
        i = next(k for k in range(min(len(back), len(data)))
                 if back[k] != data[k]) if len(back) == len(data) else -1
        return f"{name}: ENC mismatch at byte {i} (len {len(back)} vs {len(data)})"
    # 2. my decode must invert reference decode's result back to identity,
    #    and must match the reference inverse: my_decode(ref_decode(x)) == x
    rd = ref_decode(data, **kw)
    d = my_run(rd, "dec", **kw)
    if d != data:
        i = next(k for k in range(min(len(d), len(data)))
                 if d[k] != data[k]) if len(d) == len(data) else -1
        return f"{name}: DEC mismatch at byte {i}"
    # 3. self round-trip
    if my_run(e, "dec", **kw) != data:
        return f"{name}: self round-trip failed"
    return None

def report(err):
    if err:
        print("FAIL:", err)
    return err is None

# 02 — Option Parsing & Exit Codes (capture prefix `opt`)

Reference binary: `/workspace/executable` (xz 5.8.2). All captures made with `LC_ALL=C`.
Raw captures: `/tmp/xztest/ref/opt_*.out` / `opt_*.err` (one pair per command; names referenced per test).
Scratch dir with fixtures: `/tmp/xzprobe_opt`.

**Global conventions observed:**

- Every diagnostic message goes to **stderr**; stdout carries only payload data (or `--version`/`--help` text).
- Messages are prefixed with the program name **exactly as invoked** (argv[0]): all captures below show `/workspace/executable: ` because that is how it was run. A clone should substitute its own argv[0].
- Whitespace verified with `sed -n l`: every message line ends with a single `\n`; **no trailing spaces**; long lines (e.g. ambiguous-option candidate lists) are a **single physical line**, never wrapped.
- Exit codes seen: `0` success, `1` any error, `2` "warning(s) only" (details in Scope B).

Machine facts for this capture host: 64 CPU cores (`nproc`), MemTotal 131882676 kB. Machine-dependent outputs are flagged **[machine-dependent]**.

---

## Scope A — Option parsing

### A.1 Unrecognized options

**`LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable -y`** → exit **1** (`opt_unrec_short`)

stdout: empty

stderr:
```
/workspace/executable: invalid option -- 'y'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable --frobnicate`** → exit **1** (`opt_unrec_long`)

stdout: empty

stderr:
```
/workspace/executable: unrecognized option '--frobnicate'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

Notes:

- Short-option message format: `PROG: invalid option -- 'X'` (this is the glibc getopt message, printed by getopt itself).
- Long-option message: `PROG: unrecognized option '--NAME'` (also getopt's own).
- Both are followed by xz's own hint line: `PROG: Try 'PROG --help' for more information.`
- The getopt line is **never** suppressible (not even by `-qq`, see B.6). The `Try ...` hint line **is** suppressed if `-q` was already parsed **before** the bad option:

**`LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable -q -y`** → exit **1** (`opt_unrec_q`)

stderr (note: no `Try` line):
```
/workspace/executable: invalid option -- 'y'
```

**`LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable -y -q`** → exit **1** (`opt_unrec_yafter`)

stderr (hint printed, because `-q` comes after the error):
```
/workspace/executable: invalid option -- 'y'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

### A.2 Long-option abbreviations (unambiguous prefixes ARE accepted)

Abbreviation resolution follows GNU getopt_long rules: any unique prefix is accepted; a prefix matching more than one option fails with an "ambiguous" message listing ALL candidates, each in single quotes, space-separated, in the option table's order. Unambiguous abbreviations behave identically to the full name.

Accepted (exit 0):

- **`/workspace/executable --vers`** → exit **0** (`opt_abbrev_vers`). stderr empty; stdout:
```
xz (XZ Utils) 5.8.2
liblzma 5.8.2
```
- **`/workspace/executable --std plain.txt`** → exit **0**, compresses to stdout (works as `--stdout`). Binary .xz stream on stdout: 68 B, MD5 38c3e6215ed1cbf299e8b617e9a52076 (input was `hi\n`). stderr empty. (`opt_abbrev_std`)
- **`/workspace/executable --st plain.txt`** → exit **0**, identical output (MD5 38c3e6215ed1cbf299e8b617e9a52076). (`opt_abbrev_st`)
- **`/workspace/executable --q plain.txt -c`** → exit **0**, works as `--quiet`; normal .xz output on stdout (68 B). (`opt_abbrev_q`)
- **`/workspace/executable --memlimit-c`** resolves uniquely to `--memlimit-compress` (it then fails for missing argument — see A.3).

Ambiguous (all exit **1**, stdout empty):

**`/workspace/executable --ver`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_ver`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--ver' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--verbose' '--version'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --v`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_v`) — same candidates:
```
/workspace/executable: option '--v' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--verbose' '--version'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --b`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_b`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--b' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--block-size' '--block-list' '--best'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --fo`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_fo`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--fo' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--force' '--format'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --f`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_f`) — the candidate list is ONE physical line:
```
/workspace/executable: option '--f' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--force' '--files' '--files0' '--format' '--flush-timeout' '--fast' '--filters' '--filters1' '--filters2' '--filters3' '--filters4' '--filters5' '--filters6' '--filters7' '--filters8' '--filters9' '--filters-help'

### A.4 Invalid numeric arguments

Two distinct error shapes (both exit **1**, stdout empty, and NOTE: **no `Try ...` hint line** is printed for these — they are xz's own argument-validation messages, not getopt's):

1. Non-numeric / negative: `PROG: ARG: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer`
2. Bad suffix after valid digits: two lines —
```
PROG: TAIL: Invalid multiplier suffix
PROG: Valid suffixes are 'KiB' (2^10), 'MiB' (2^20), and 'GiB' (2^30).

| `-T -1 plain.txt` | 1 | `-1: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_Tneg1` |
| `-T0x plain.txt` | 1 | `x: Invalid multiplier suffix` + suffix-help line | `opt_num_T0x` |
| `--block-size=xyz plain.txt` | 1 | `xyz: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_bsxyz` |
| `--block-size=-5 plain.txt` | 1 | `-5: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_bsneg5` |
| `--block-size=1.5MiB plain.txt` | 1 | `.5MiB: Invalid multiplier suffix` + suffix-help line | `opt_num_bs15` |
| `--memlimit-compress=abc plain.txt` | 1 | `abc: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_memabc` |
| `--memlimit-compress=-1 plain.txt` | 1 | `-1: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_memneg` |

Verbatim example (`opt_num_T0x`.err):
```

/workspace/executable: Valid suffixes are 'KiB' (2^10), 'MiB' (2^20), and 'GiB' (2^30).
```

Overflow / out-of-range (third message shape, exit **1**):

**`/workspace/executable --block-size=99999999999999999999999999 plain.txt`** (`opt_num_bsover`):

```

**`/workspace/executable -T 99999999999999999999999999 plain.txt`** (`opt_num_Tover`):

/workspace/executable: Value of the option 'threads' must be in the range [0, 16384]

### A.5 Preset options (`-0`…`-9`, grouping, `-e`)

Presets are parsed as individual short options; digits can be grouped and the LAST one wins. Verified by output identity (input `hello world\n`, 12 B; `-kc` to stdout):

| Command | Exit | stdout MD5 | Identical to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-1` | 0 | 79aeee0d9e2bd12e9ead8d6c2bfa20f4 | `-9 -1`, `-91`-style grouping |
| `-9` | 0 | f17a7b3103bd939759e0a5ffcaa52e81 | `-19`, `-1 -9`, `-99` |
| `-0` | 0 | 0815feda37a1e3e99d2961185372daf3 | `-10` |
| `-19` | 0 | f17a7b3103bd939759e0a5ffcaa52e81 | = `-1 -9` → last (`-9`) wins |
| `-99` | 0 | f17a7b3103bd939759e0a5ffcaa52e81 | = `-9 -9` → `-9` |
| `-10` | 0 | 0815feda37a1e3e99d2961185372daf3 | = `-1 -0` → `-0`; **`-10` is NOT an error** |
| `-9e` / `-e9` | 0 | f17a7b3103bd939759e0a5ffcaa52e81 | `-e` mixes freely into the group |

(Captures `opt_preset_0/1/9/10/19/19b/91/99/9e/e9`.)

### A.6 `--` end-of-options; option-like filenames; lone `-`

Fixture: file named `-foo` containing `dashfile\n` in the cwd.

**`/workspace/executable -kc -- -foo`** → exit **0** (`opt_dashdash`): `-foo` treated as a filename; .xz stream on stdout (76 B, MD5 ab897a44c57fa3a540f21ef978d6d520). stderr empty.

**`/workspace/executable -kc ./-foo`** → exit **0** (`opt_dotdash`): same output (MD5 ab897a44c57fa3a540f21ef978d6d520) — `./-foo` works without `--`.

**`/workspace/executable -c -foo`** (no `--`) → exit **1** (`opt_nodash`): parsed as options `-f -o -o`; `-o` is unknown:
```
/workspace/executable: invalid option -- 'o'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable -- -foo -c`** → exit **1** (`opt_dashdash_optafter`): EVERYTHING after `--` is a filename. `-foo` was compressed in place (creating `-foo.xz`; on a rerun with `-foo.xz` already present it instead reports `-foo.xz: File exists`), then `-c` is treated as a filename:
```
/workspace/executable: -foo.xz: File exists
/workspace/executable: -c: No such file or directory
```
(First run, without pre-existing `-foo.xz`, printed only `/workspace/executable: -c: No such file or directory`, exit 1. Both messages on stderr; exit 1 either way. Nonexistent-file message shape: `PROG: NAME: No such file or directory`; existing-target message: `PROG: NAME.xz: File exists`.)

**Lone `-` means stdin** (and stdout, since input is stdin):

- **`printf 'hello world\n' | /workspace/executable -`** → exit **0** (`opt_lone_dash`): compressed .xz on stdout (76 B, MD5 151c72adeac49d68ba2d59d105599486). stderr empty.

- **`/workspace/executable -d - < opt_lone_dash.out`** → exit **0** (`opt_lone_dash_d`): stdout is `hello world\n`; stderr empty.

## Scope B — Exit codes (0 / 1 / 2), warnings, `-q`/`-qq`, `-Q`/`--no-warn`

### B.1 Rules (verified below)

- **0** — success, no warnings.
- **1** — at least one error (with or without warnings). Confirmed for: option errors, numeric errors, missing files, corrupt data, trailing garbage, format not recognized.
- **2** — warning(s) only, no errors. The canonical warning is an unsupported integrity-check type on decompression/test.
- `-q`/`-qq` only change MESSAGE VERBOSITY, **never exit codes** (a suppressed warning still yields 2; a suppressed error still yields 1).
- `-Q`/`--no-warn` does NOT suppress the warning message; it makes warnings not affect the exit code (2 → 0). It has no effect on errors.
- CAUTION for clone authors: not every warning-verbosity message sets exit 2 — the memlimit "Switching to single-threaded mode" notices are suppressed by `-q` but leave the exit code 0 (B.8). Exit 2 is tied to specific warning conditions (unsupported check observed), not to message level.

### B.2 Test fixtures (all in `/tmp/xzprobe_opt`)

- `data.txt` = `The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\n` (45 B).
- `good.xz` = `/workspace/executable -kc data.txt` (112 B, default `-6`, CRC64).
- `badcheck3.xz` — **unsupported check, well-formed**: made from `--check=crc32` output (108 B) by patching the check ID `0x01`→`0x02` (reserved, same 4-byte size per xz-file-format.txt §2.1.1.2) in BOTH stream headers and fixing both CRC32s:
  - header: byte 7 → `0x02`; bytes 8–11 → LE CRC32 of bytes 6–7.
  - footer: byte at `len-3` (2nd stream-flags byte) → `0x02`; bytes `len-12..len-9` → LE CRC32 of bytes `len-8..len-3`.
  - Patched header bytes: `fd 37 7a 58 5a 00 00 02 d3 73 d7 af`; footer: `2a 13 90 94 01 00 00 00 00 02 59 5a`.
- `garbage.xz` = `good.xz` + 21 bytes `GARBAGE-TRAILING-JUNK`.
- `garbage4.xz` = `good.xz` + 4 bytes `JUNK` (multiple of 4, but nonzero → invalid padding).
- `pad4.xz` = `good.xz` + 4 NUL bytes (valid stream padding).
- `garbmagic.xz` = `good.xz` + `fd 37 7a 58 5a 00` + `junkjunk` (valid xz magic, then junk).
- `concat2.xz` = `good.xz` + `good.xz` (two valid concatenated streams).
- `badcrc64.xz` = `good.xz` with the 8-byte CRC64 check field (the 8 bytes immediately preceding the index) XORed with 0xFF.
- `badcheck.xz` / `badcheck2.xz` — FAILED craft attempts (check ID 0x0F, a 64-byte reserved check, on CRC64/None bases whose check fields aren't 64 bytes): these decode the payload but then report an error. Kept for reference; see B.3 note.

### B.3 Unsupported integrity check → warning, exit 2

**`/workspace/executable -dc badcheck3.xz`** → exit **2** (`opt_badcheck3_d`)

stdout (full payload still produced):
```
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
```
stderr:
```
/workspace/executable: badcheck3.xz: Unsupported type of integrity check; not verifying file integrity
```

**`/workspace/executable -t badcheck3.xz`** → exit **2** (`opt_badcheck3_t`)

stdout: empty. stderr: same single warning line as above.

**`/workspace/executable -dc --ignore-check badcheck3.xz`** → exit **0** (`opt_badcheck3_ig`)

stdout: full payload. stderr: **empty** — `--ignore-check` both silences this warning and yields exit 0.

Note on the failed crafts (`badcheck.xz`, `badcheck2.xz`, check ID `0x0F` = reserved 64-byte check on a file whose check field is shorter): the payload is decoded and written, the same `Unsupported type of integrity check; not verifying file integrity` warning appears, but it is FOLLOWED by an error `PROG: FILE: Unexpected end of input` and exit is **1** (captures `opt_badcheck_d/t/ig`, `opt_badcheck2_d/t/ig/tig`). With `--ignore-check` only the warning vanishes; the `Unexpected end of input` error and exit 1 remain. Moral: the check-field size implied by the check ID must match the file, or the warning degrades into an error.

### B.4 Trailing garbage after a valid stream → error, exit 1 (NOT a warning)

**`/workspace/executable -dc garbage.xz`** → exit **1** (`opt_garbage_d`)

stdout: full 45 B payload of the first stream (already written before the error).
stderr:
```
/workspace/executable: garbage.xz: Compressed data is corrupt
```

**`/workspace/executable -t garbage.xz`** → exit **1** (`opt_garbage_t`): stdout empty, same stderr message.

**`/workspace/executable -dc --format=xz garbage.xz`** → exit **1** (`opt_garbage_fmtxz`): identical message — `Compressed data is corrupt`.

**`/workspace/executable -dc garbage4.xz`** (4 junk bytes, 4-aligned) → exit **1** (`opt_garbage4_d`), payload produced, DIFFERENT message:
```
/workspace/executable: garbage4.xz: Unexpected end of input
```
(4 aligned nonzero bytes are read as the start of a new stream header, then EOF hits.)

**`/workspace/executable -dc garbmagic.xz`** (xz magic + junk) → exit **1** (`opt_garbmagic_d`):
```
/workspace/executable: garbmagic.xz: Compressed data is corrupt
```

Controls:

- **`/workspace/executable -dc pad4.xz`** (4 NUL bytes = legal stream padding) → exit **0**, payload produced, stderr empty (`opt_pad4_d`).
- **`/workspace/executable -dc concat2.xz`** (two valid streams) → exit **0**, stdout = payload twice (90 B), stderr empty (`opt_concat2_d`).
- **`/workspace/executable -dc plain2.txt`** (plain text, not compressed) → exit **1** (`opt_notxz_d`):
```
/workspace/executable: plain2.txt: File format not recognized
```
Same with `--format=xz` (`opt_notxz_fmtxz`, exit 1).

### B.5 Corrupt check field vs `--ignore-check`

**`/workspace/executable -t badcrc64.xz`** → exit **1** (`opt_badcrc_t`):
```
/workspace/executable: badcrc64.xz: Compressed data is corrupt
```
(A bad CRC64 in a SUPPORTED check type is a hard error, not a warning — no exit 2 here.)

**`/workspace/executable -t --ignore-check badcrc64.xz`** → exit **0**, stdout empty, stderr empty (`opt_badcrc_tig`).

**`/workspace/executable -dc --ignore-check badcrc64.xz`** → exit **0**, full payload on stdout, stderr empty (`opt_badcrc_dig`).

### B.6 `-q` / `-qq`: message suppression only, exit codes unchanged

On the warning case `badcheck3.xz`:

| Command | Exit | stdout | stderr | Capture |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-q -dc badcheck3.xz` | **2** | payload (45 B) | empty (warning suppressed) | `opt_bc3_q` |
| `-qq -dc badcheck3.xz` | **2** | payload (45 B) | empty | `opt_bc3_qq` |
| `-v -dc badcheck3.xz` | **2** | payload | warning + `badcheck3.xz: 108 B / 45 B = 2.400` | `opt_bc3_v` |
| `-vv -dc badcheck3.xz` | **2** | payload | same as `-v` here | `opt_bc3_vv` |

So `-q` (once) hides warnings but the exit code STAYS 2.

On error cases:

| Command | Exit | stderr | Capture |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-q -dc garbage.xz` | 1 | `/workspace/executable: garbage.xz: Compressed data is corrupt` | `opt_gar_q` |
| `-qq -dc garbage.xz` | 1 | **empty** | `opt_gar_qq` |
| `-dc nosuchfile.xz` | 1 | `/workspace/executable: nosuchfile.xz: No such file or directory` | `opt_missf` |
| `-q -dc nosuchfile.xz` | 1 | same message shown | `opt_missf_q` |
| `-qq -dc nosuchfile.xz` | 1 | **empty** | `opt_missf_qq` |
| `-q -T foo` | 1 | `/workspace/executable: foo: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_numerr_q` |
| `-qq -T foo` | 1 | **empty** | `opt_numerr_qq` |

Summary: default = warnings+errors shown; `-q` = errors only; `-qq` = neither. **Exit codes are unaffected by `-q`/`-qq`.**

Exceptions that are NEVER suppressed:

- getopt's own first line (`invalid option -- 'x'`, `unrecognized option '--foo'`, `option requires an argument -- 'T'`) prints even under `-qq` (`opt_unrec_qq`, `opt_unrec_qqfirst`):
```
/workspace/executable: unrecognized option '--frobnicate'
```
- But xz's `Try '... --help' for more information.` companion line IS suppressed once `-q` has been parsed (A.1).

### B.7 `-Q` / `--no-warn`: keeps the message, drops exit 2 to 0

| Command | Exit | stderr | Capture |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Q -dc badcheck3.xz` | **0** | warning STILL printed: `/workspace/executable: badcheck3.xz: Unsupported type of integrity check; not verifying file integrity` | `opt_bc3_Q` |
| `--no-warn -dc badcheck3.xz` | **0** | same warning printed | `opt_bc3_nowarn` |
| `-Q -t badcheck3.xz` | **0** | same warning printed | `opt_bc3_Qt` |
| `-Q -q -dc badcheck3.xz` | 0 | empty | `opt_bc3_Qq` |
| `-Q -qq -dc badcheck3.xz` | 0 | empty | `opt_bc3_Qqq` |
| `-Q -v -dc badcheck3.xz` | 0 | warning + verbose line `badcheck3.xz: 108 B / 45 B = 2.400` | `opt_bc3_Qv` |
| `-Q -dc garbage.xz` (error case) | **1** | `/workspace/executable: garbage.xz: Compressed data is corrupt` | `opt_gar_Q` |
| `-Q -dc nosuchfile.xz` (error case) | **1** | `... No such file or directory` | `opt_missf_Q` |

So `--no-warn` = "do not set exit status 2 on warnings"; it neither hides messages nor touches errors. `-v` and `-Q` combine freely (`-Qv`: verbose output printed, warning printed, exit 0).

With a memory limit too low for threaded compression:

**`/workspace/executable -T64 --memlimit-compress=100MiB -kc plain.txt`** → exit **0** (`opt_thr_reduce`)

stdout: valid .xz (68 B). stderr:

```

**`/workspace/executable -T8 --memlimit-compress=50MiB -kc plain.txt`** → exit **0** (`opt_thr_reduce2`), stderr:

### B.10 Machine-dependent observations (64-core host, ~125.8 GiB RAM)

- `-T0` means "auto = number of CPU cores". Verbose evidence — **`/workspace/executable -T0 -vv -kc plain.txt`** → exit 0 (`opt_T0_vv`), stdout 76 B .xz, stderr:
```

/workspace/executable: Using up to 64 threads.
/workspace/executable: 10567 MiB of memory is required. The limiter is disabled.
/workspace/executable: Decompression will need 9 MiB of memory.
plain.txt: 76 B / 12 B = 6.333
```
`Using up to 64 threads.` = nproc of this host **[machine-dependent]**. The `10567 MiB` figure scales with the thread count (hence also machine-dependent); `Decompression will need 9 MiB` depends only on the filter chain. The last line (`NAME: COMPRESSED B / UNCOMPRESSED B = RATIO`) is the standard `-v` summary on stderr; note it has NO program-name prefix, unlike diagnostics.
- `-T` hard maximum is 16384 threads on this build (A.4), independent of core count.

# 02 — Option Parsing & Exit Codes (capture prefix `opt`)

Reference binary: `/workspace/executable` (xz 5.8.2). All captures made with `LC_ALL=C`.
Raw captures: `/tmp/xztest/ref/opt_*.out` / `opt_*.err` (one pair per command; names referenced per test).
Scratch dir with fixtures: `/tmp/xzprobe_opt`.

**Global conventions observed:**

- Every diagnostic message goes to **stderr**; stdout carries only payload data (or `--version`/`--help` text).
- Messages are prefixed with the program name **exactly as invoked** (argv[0]): all captures below show `/workspace/executable: ` because that is how it was run. A clone should substitute its own argv[0].
- Whitespace verified with `sed -n l`: every message line ends with a single `\n`; **no trailing spaces**; long lines (e.g. ambiguous-option candidate lists) are a **single physical line**, never wrapped.
- Exit codes seen: `0` success, `1` any error, `2` "warning(s) only" (details in Scope B).

Machine facts for this capture host: 64 CPU cores (`nproc`), MemTotal 131882676 kB. Machine-dependent outputs are flagged **[machine-dependent]**.

---

## Scope A — Option parsing

### A.1 Unrecognized options

**`LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable -y`** → exit **1** (`opt_unrec_short`)

stdout: empty

stderr:
```
/workspace/executable: invalid option -- 'y'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable --frobnicate`** → exit **1** (`opt_unrec_long`)

stdout: empty

stderr:
```
/workspace/executable: unrecognized option '--frobnicate'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

Notes:

- Short-option message format: `PROG: invalid option -- 'X'` (this is the glibc getopt message, printed by getopt itself).
- Long-option message: `PROG: unrecognized option '--NAME'` (also getopt's own).
- Both are followed by xz's own hint line: `PROG: Try 'PROG --help' for more information.`
- The getopt line is **never** suppressible (not even by `-qq`, see B.6). The `Try ...` hint line **is** suppressed if `-q` was already parsed **before** the bad option:

**`LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable -q -y`** → exit **1** (`opt_unrec_q`)

stderr (note: no `Try` line):
```
/workspace/executable: invalid option -- 'y'
```

**`LC_ALL=C /workspace/executable -y -q`** → exit **1** (`opt_unrec_yafter`)

stderr (hint printed, because `-q` comes after the error):
```
/workspace/executable: invalid option -- 'y'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

### A.2 Long-option abbreviations (unambiguous prefixes ARE accepted)

Abbreviation resolution follows GNU getopt_long rules: any unique prefix is accepted; a prefix matching more than one option fails with an "ambiguous" message listing ALL candidates, each in single quotes, space-separated, in the option table's order. Unambiguous abbreviations behave identically to the full name.

Accepted (exit 0):

- **`/workspace/executable --vers`** → exit **0** (`opt_abbrev_vers`). stderr empty; stdout:
```
xz (XZ Utils) 5.8.2
liblzma 5.8.2
```
- **`/workspace/executable --std plain.txt`** → exit **0**, compresses to stdout (works as `--stdout`). Binary .xz stream on stdout: 68 B, MD5 38c3e6215ed1cbf299e8b617e9a52076 (input was `hi\n`). stderr empty. (`opt_abbrev_std`)
- **`/workspace/executable --st plain.txt`** → exit **0**, identical output (MD5 38c3e6215ed1cbf299e8b617e9a52076). (`opt_abbrev_st`)
- **`/workspace/executable --q plain.txt -c`** → exit **0**, works as `--quiet`; normal .xz output on stdout (68 B). (`opt_abbrev_q`)
- **`/workspace/executable --memlimit-c`** resolves uniquely to `--memlimit-compress` (it then fails for missing argument — see A.3).

Ambiguous (all exit **1**, stdout empty):

**`/workspace/executable --ver`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_ver`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--ver' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--verbose' '--version'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --v`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_v`) — same candidates:
```
/workspace/executable: option '--v' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--verbose' '--version'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --b`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_b`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--b' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--block-size' '--block-list' '--best'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --fo`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_fo`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--fo' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--force' '--format'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --f`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_f`) — the candidate list is ONE physical line:
```
/workspace/executable: option '--f' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--force' '--files' '--files0' '--format' '--flush-timeout' '--fast' '--filters' '--filters1' '--filters2' '--filters3' '--filters4' '--filters5' '--filters6' '--filters7' '--filters8' '--filters9' '--filters-help'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --de`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_de`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--de' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--decompress' '--delta'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --no`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_no`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--no' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--no-sync' '--no-sparse' '--no-adjust' '--no-warn'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --mem`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_mem`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--mem' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--memlimit-compress' '--memlimit-decompress' '--memlimit-mt-decompress' '--memlimit' '--memory'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```
(Note: both `--memlimit` and `--memory` exist as full option names in 5.8.2.)

**`/workspace/executable --c`** → exit 1 (`opt_abbrev_c`)
```
/workspace/executable: option '--c' is ambiguous; possibilities: '--compress' '--check'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

### A.3 Missing option arguments

All exit **1**, stdout empty.

**`/workspace/executable --block-size`** (`opt_missarg_blocksize`):
```
/workspace/executable: option '--block-size' requires an argument
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --memlimit-compress`** (`opt_missarg_memcomp`):
```
/workspace/executable: option '--memlimit-compress' requires an argument
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --memlimit`** (`opt_abbrev_memlimit` — full option `--memlimit` exists):
```
/workspace/executable: option '--memlimit' requires an argument
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --memlimit-c`** (`opt_abbrev_memlimitc` — unique abbreviation of `--memlimit-compress`):
```
/workspace/executable: option '--memlimit-compress' requires an argument
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```
(Note: the message names the RESOLVED full option, not the abbreviation typed.)

**`/workspace/executable --block-list`** (`opt_missarg_blocklist`):
```
/workspace/executable: option '--block-list' requires an argument
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable --format`** (`opt_missarg_format`):
```
/workspace/executable: option '--format' requires an argument
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable -T`** (short option, end of argv) (`opt_missarg_T`) — different message shape (getopt's own):
```
/workspace/executable: option requires an argument -- 'T'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**Argument consumption from the next argv word:** options with required arguments take the following argv word even if it looks like an option.

**`/workspace/executable -T -9 plain.txt -c`** → exit **1** (`opt_missarg_T_nextopt`): `-9` is eaten as `-T`'s argument and then fails numeric parsing:
```
/workspace/executable: -9: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer
```

**`/workspace/executable --threads -kc plain.txt`** → exit **1** (`opt_threads`):
```
/workspace/executable: -kc: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer
```

**`/workspace/executable --block-size 4096 -c plain.txt`** → exit **0** (`opt_separg_blocksize`): long options also accept a SEPARATE next-word argument (no `=` needed). Binary .xz stream on stdout: 64 B, MD5 375c85fb1cefe8c3edb7ec0ce7194d5d.

**`/workspace/executable -T=4 -kc plain.txt`** → exit **1** (`opt_num_Teq4`): for SHORT options there is no `=` syntax; `=4` becomes the argument verbatim:
```
/workspace/executable: =4: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer
```

**`/workspace/executable --threads=4 -kc plain.txt`** → exit **0** (`opt_threads_eq`; 76 B .xz on stdout, stderr empty).

### A.4 Invalid numeric arguments

Two distinct error shapes (both exit **1**, stdout empty, and NOTE: **no `Try ...` hint line** is printed for these — they are xz's own argument-validation messages, not getopt's):

1. Non-numeric / negative: `PROG: ARG: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer`
2. Bad suffix after valid digits: two lines —
```
PROG: TAIL: Invalid multiplier suffix
PROG: Valid suffixes are 'KiB' (2^10), 'MiB' (2^20), and 'GiB' (2^30).
```
The reported token is the UNPARSED TAIL (digits already consumed are stripped).

Individual results:

| Command | Exit | stderr (after `PROG: ` prefix) | Capture |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-T foo plain.txt` | 1 | `foo: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_Tfoo` |
| `-T -1 plain.txt` | 1 | `-1: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_Tneg1` |
| `-T0x plain.txt` | 1 | `x: Invalid multiplier suffix` + suffix-help line | `opt_num_T0x` |
| `--block-size=xyz plain.txt` | 1 | `xyz: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_bsxyz` |
| `--block-size=-5 plain.txt` | 1 | `-5: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_bsneg5` |
| `--block-size=1.5MiB plain.txt` | 1 | `.5MiB: Invalid multiplier suffix` + suffix-help line | `opt_num_bs15` |
| `--memlimit-compress=abc plain.txt` | 1 | `abc: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_memabc` |
| `--memlimit-compress=-1 plain.txt` | 1 | `-1: Value is not a non-negative decimal integer` | `opt_num_memneg` |

Verbatim example (`opt_num_T0x`.err):
```
/workspace/executable: x: Invalid multiplier suffix
/workspace/executable: Valid suffixes are 'KiB' (2^10), 'MiB' (2^20), and 'GiB' (2^30).
```

Overflow / out-of-range (third message shape, exit **1**):

**`/workspace/executable --block-size=99999999999999999999999999 plain.txt`** (`opt_num_bsover`):
```
/workspace/executable: Value of the option 'block-size' must be in the range [0, 9223372036854775807]
```

**`/workspace/executable -T 99999999999999999999999999 plain.txt`** (`opt_num_Tover`):
```
/workspace/executable: Value of the option 'threads' must be in the range [0, 16384]
```

**`/workspace/executable --memlimit-compress=99999999999999999999999 plain.txt`** (`opt_num_memover`):
```
/workspace/executable: Value of the option 'memlimit-compress' must be in the range [0, 18446744073709551615]
```

Range boundaries verified:

- `-T 16384` → exit **0** (`opt_num_T16384`); `-T 16385` → exit **1** with the `[0, 16384]` message above (`opt_num_T16385`). Thread count is capped at 16384 regardless of the 64-core host.
- `--memlimit-compress` range is full uint64: `[0, 18446744073709551615]`.
- `--block-size` range is int64: `[0, 9223372036854775807]`.

Accepted spellings (all exit **0**, stderr empty):

- `--memlimit-compress=50%` — percent suffix accepted (`opt_num_mempct`).
- `--block-size=0` — zero accepted (`opt_num_bs0`; output identical to default single-block for tiny input, MD5 151c72adeac49d68ba2d59d105599486).
- `--block-size=1KiB` — suffix accepted, case as shown (`opt_num_bs1kib`).

### A.5 Preset options (`-0`…`-9`, grouping, `-e`)

Presets are parsed as individual short options; digits can be grouped and the LAST one wins. Verified by output identity (input `hello world\n`, 12 B; `-kc` to stdout):

| Command | Exit | stdout MD5 | Identical to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-1` | 0 | 79aeee0d9e2bd12e9ead8d6c2bfa20f4 | `-9 -1`, `-91`-style grouping |
| `-9` | 0 | f17a7b3103bd939759e0a5ffcaa52e81 | `-19`, `-1 -9`, `-99` |
| `-0` | 0 | 0815feda37a1e3e99d2961185372daf3 | `-10` |
| `-19` | 0 | f17a7b3103bd939759e0a5ffcaa52e81 | = `-1 -9` → last (`-9`) wins |
| `-99` | 0 | f17a7b3103bd939759e0a5ffcaa52e81 | = `-9 -9` → `-9` |
| `-10` | 0 | 0815feda37a1e3e99d2961185372daf3 | = `-1 -0` → `-0`; **`-10` is NOT an error** |
| `-9e` / `-e9` | 0 | f17a7b3103bd939759e0a5ffcaa52e81 | `-e` mixes freely into the group |

(Captures `opt_preset_0/1/9/10/19/19b/91/99/9e/e9`.)

**`/workspace/executable -0x plain.txt`** → exit **1** (`opt_preset_0x`): after `-0`, `x` is parsed as another short option:
```
/workspace/executable: invalid option -- 'x'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

### A.6 `--` end-of-options; option-like filenames; lone `-`

Fixture: file named `-foo` containing `dashfile\n` in the cwd.

**`/workspace/executable -kc -- -foo`** → exit **0** (`opt_dashdash`): `-foo` treated as a filename; .xz stream on stdout (76 B, MD5 ab897a44c57fa3a540f21ef978d6d520). stderr empty.

**`/workspace/executable -kc ./-foo`** → exit **0** (`opt_dotdash`): same output (MD5 ab897a44c57fa3a540f21ef978d6d520) — `./-foo` works without `--`.

**`/workspace/executable -c -foo`** (no `--`) → exit **1** (`opt_nodash`): parsed as options `-f -o -o`; `-o` is unknown:
```
/workspace/executable: invalid option -- 'o'
/workspace/executable: Try '/workspace/executable --help' for more information.
```

**`/workspace/executable -- -foo -c`** → exit **1** (`opt_dashdash_optafter`): EVERYTHING after `--` is a filename. `-foo` was compressed in place (creating `-foo.xz`; on a rerun with `-foo.xz` already present it instead reports `-foo.xz: File exists`), then `-c` is treated as a filename:
```
/workspace/executable: -foo.xz: File exists
/workspace/executable: -c: No such file or directory
```
(First run, without pre-existing `-foo.xz`, printed only `/workspace/executable: -c: No such file or directory`, exit 1. Both messages on stderr; exit 1 either way. Nonexistent-file message shape: `PROG: NAME: No such file or directory`; existing-target message: `PROG: NAME.xz: File exists`.)

**Lone `-` means stdin** (and stdout, since input is stdin):

- **`printf 'hello world\n' | /workspace/executable -`** → exit **0** (`opt_lone_dash`): compressed .xz on stdout (76 B, MD5 151c72adeac49d68ba2d59d105599486). stderr empty.
- **`printf 'hello world\n' | /workspace/executable -c -`** → exit **0**, identical output (`opt_lone_dash_c`).
- **`/workspace/executable -d - < opt_lone_dash.out`** → exit **0** (`opt_lone_dash_d`): stdout is `hello world\n`; stderr empty.

### A.7 `--help` / `--version` exit codes

- `/workspace/executable --help` → exit **0** (`opt_help_rc`; stdout 1517 B — content covered by sibling section 01).
- `/workspace/executable --version` → exit **0** (`opt_version_rc`; stdout 34 B, identical to `--vers` output in A.2).

---

## Scope B — Exit codes (0 / 1 / 2), warnings, `-q`/`-qq`, `-Q`/`--no-warn`

### B.1 Rules (verified below)

- **0** — success, no warnings.
- **1** — at least one error (with or without warnings). Confirmed for: option errors, numeric errors, missing files, corrupt data, trailing garbage, format not recognized.
- **2** — warning(s) only, no errors. The canonical warning is an unsupported integrity-check type on decompression/test.
- `-q`/`-qq` only change MESSAGE VERBOSITY, **never exit codes** (a suppressed warning still yields 2; a suppressed error still yields 1).
- `-Q`/`--no-warn` does NOT suppress the warning message; it makes warnings not affect the exit code (2 → 0). It has no effect on errors.
- CAUTION for clone authors: not every warning-verbosity message sets exit 2 — the memlimit "Switching to single-threaded mode" notices are suppressed by `-q` but leave the exit code 0 (B.8). Exit 2 is tied to specific warning conditions (unsupported check observed), not to message level.

### B.2 Test fixtures (all in `/tmp/xzprobe_opt`)

- `data.txt` = `The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\n` (45 B).
- `good.xz` = `/workspace/executable -kc data.txt` (112 B, default `-6`, CRC64).
- `badcheck3.xz` — **unsupported check, well-formed**: made from `--check=crc32` output (108 B) by patching the check ID `0x01`→`0x02` (reserved, same 4-byte size per xz-file-format.txt §2.1.1.2) in BOTH stream headers and fixing both CRC32s:
  - header: byte 7 → `0x02`; bytes 8–11 → LE CRC32 of bytes 6–7.
  - footer: byte at `len-3` (2nd stream-flags byte) → `0x02`; bytes `len-12..len-9` → LE CRC32 of bytes `len-8..len-3`.
  - Patched header bytes: `fd 37 7a 58 5a 00 00 02 d3 73 d7 af`; footer: `2a 13 90 94 01 00 00 00 00 02 59 5a`.
- `garbage.xz` = `good.xz` + 21 bytes `GARBAGE-TRAILING-JUNK`.
- `garbage4.xz` = `good.xz` + 4 bytes `JUNK` (multiple of 4, but nonzero → invalid padding).
- `pad4.xz` = `good.xz` + 4 NUL bytes (valid stream padding).
- `garbmagic.xz` = `good.xz` + `fd 37 7a 58 5a 00` + `junkjunk` (valid xz magic, then junk).
- `concat2.xz` = `good.xz` + `good.xz` (two valid concatenated streams).
- `badcrc64.xz` = `good.xz` with the 8-byte CRC64 check field (the 8 bytes immediately preceding the index) XORed with 0xFF.
- `badcheck.xz` / `badcheck2.xz` — FAILED craft attempts (check ID 0x0F, a 64-byte reserved check, on CRC64/None bases whose check fields aren't 64 bytes): these decode the payload but then report an error. Kept for reference; see B.3 note.

### B.3 Unsupported integrity check → warning, exit 2

**`/workspace/executable -dc badcheck3.xz`** → exit **2** (`opt_badcheck3_d`)

stdout (full payload still produced):
```
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
```
stderr:
```
/workspace/executable: badcheck3.xz: Unsupported type of integrity check; not verifying file integrity
```

**`/workspace/executable -t badcheck3.xz`** → exit **2** (`opt_badcheck3_t`)

stdout: empty. stderr: same single warning line as above.

**`/workspace/executable -dc --ignore-check badcheck3.xz`** → exit **0** (`opt_badcheck3_ig`)

stdout: full payload. stderr: **empty** — `--ignore-check` both silences this warning and yields exit 0.

Note on the failed crafts (`badcheck.xz`, `badcheck2.xz`, check ID `0x0F` = reserved 64-byte check on a file whose check field is shorter): the payload is decoded and written, the same `Unsupported type of integrity check; not verifying file integrity` warning appears, but it is FOLLOWED by an error `PROG: FILE: Unexpected end of input` and exit is **1** (captures `opt_badcheck_d/t/ig`, `opt_badcheck2_d/t/ig/tig`). With `--ignore-check` only the warning vanishes; the `Unexpected end of input` error and exit 1 remain. Moral: the check-field size implied by the check ID must match the file, or the warning degrades into an error.

### B.4 Trailing garbage after a valid stream → error, exit 1 (NOT a warning)

**`/workspace/executable -dc garbage.xz`** → exit **1** (`opt_garbage_d`)

stdout: full 45 B payload of the first stream (already written before the error).
stderr:
```
/workspace/executable: garbage.xz: Compressed data is corrupt
```

**`/workspace/executable -t garbage.xz`** → exit **1** (`opt_garbage_t`): stdout empty, same stderr message.

**`/workspace/executable -dc --format=xz garbage.xz`** → exit **1** (`opt_garbage_fmtxz`): identical message — `Compressed data is corrupt`.

**`/workspace/executable -dc garbage4.xz`** (4 junk bytes, 4-aligned) → exit **1** (`opt_garbage4_d`), payload produced, DIFFERENT message:
```
/workspace/executable: garbage4.xz: Unexpected end of input
```
(4 aligned nonzero bytes are read as the start of a new stream header, then EOF hits.)

**`/workspace/executable -dc garbmagic.xz`** (xz magic + junk) → exit **1** (`opt_garbmagic_d`):
```
/workspace/executable: garbmagic.xz: Compressed data is corrupt
```

Controls:

- **`/workspace/executable -dc pad4.xz`** (4 NUL bytes = legal stream padding) → exit **0**, payload produced, stderr empty (`opt_pad4_d`).
- **`/workspace/executable -dc concat2.xz`** (two valid streams) → exit **0**, stdout = payload twice (90 B), stderr empty (`opt_concat2_d`).
- **`/workspace/executable -dc plain2.txt`** (plain text, not compressed) → exit **1** (`opt_notxz_d`):
```
/workspace/executable: plain2.txt: File format not recognized
```
Same with `--format=xz` (`opt_notxz_fmtxz`, exit 1).

### B.5 Corrupt check field vs `--ignore-check`

**`/workspace/executable -t badcrc64.xz`** → exit **1** (`opt_badcrc_t`):
```
/workspace/executable: badcrc64.xz: Compressed data is corrupt
```
(A bad CRC64 in a SUPPORTED check type is a hard error, not a warning — no exit 2 here.)

**`/workspace/executable -t --ignore-check badcrc64.xz`** → exit **0**, stdout empty, stderr empty (`opt_badcrc_tig`).

**`/workspace/executable -dc --ignore-check badcrc64.xz`** → exit **0**, full payload on stdout, stderr empty (`opt_badcrc_dig`).

### B.6 `-q` / `-qq`: message suppression only, exit codes unchanged

On the warning case `badcheck3.xz`:

| Command | Exit | stdout | stderr | Capture |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-q -dc badcheck3.xz` | **2** | payload (45 B) | empty (warning suppressed) | `opt_bc3_q` |
| `-qq -dc badcheck3.xz` | **2** | payload (45 B) | empty | `opt_bc3_qq` |

With a memory limit too low for threaded compression:

**`/workspace/executable -T64 --memlimit-compress=100MiB -kc plain.txt`** → exit **0** (`opt_thr_reduce`)

# 03 — File/Usage Errors and Corruption/Format Errors (xz 5.8.2 at `/workspace/executable`) All captures were made with `LC_ALL=C`. Raw capture files live in `/tmp/xztest/ref/` with prefix `err_`; exit codes are logged in `/tmp/xzprobe_err/exitcodes.log`. **IMPORTANT — program name in messages:** every diagnostic is prefixed with argv[0] verbatim. Since the binary was invoked as `/workspace/executable`, messages begin with `/workspace/executable: `. A clone must print its own argv[0] the same way (`argv[0]: : `). Below, `PROG` denotes that prefix. **Exit-code convention observed (this scope):** - `0` = success - `1` = error (I/O errors, format errors, "File exists", tty refusal, …) - `2` = warning-level "skipping" conditions (directory, suffix, symlink, hardlink, not-a-regular-file). The file is skipped; no output produced. - When both warnings and errors occur in one invocation, the code is `1` (not observed in this scope, but worth checking in multi-file tests). All diagnostics below go to **stderr**; stdout is empty unless stated otherwise. Messages are single lines terminated by `\n` (verified with `od -c`/`sed -n l`; no trailing spaces). --- ## SCOPE A — File/usage error messages ### A.1 Nonexistent input file ``` $ xz nosuchfile.txt # exit 1 $ xz -d nosuchfile.txt.xz # exit 1 ``` stderr (both, with respective filename): ``` PROG: nosuchfile.txt: No such file or directory ``` stdout: empty. (captures: `err_a_nonexist_compress.*`, `err_a_nonexist_decompress.*`) ### A.2 Input is a directory ``` $ xz adir # exit 2 $ xz -d adir # exit 2 $ xz -f adir # exit 2 (same message; -f does NOT override) ``` stderr: ``` PROG: adir: Is a directory, skipping ``` (captures: `err_a_dir_compress.*`, `err_a_dir_decompress.*`, `err_a_dir_compress_f.*`) ### A.3 Input already has the compressor's suffix ``` $ xz foo.xz # exit 2 $ xz -S .abc foo.abc # exit 2 $ xz -f foo.xz # exit 2 — -f does NOT override this check ``` stderr: ``` PROG: foo.xz: File already has '.xz' suffix, skipping PROG: foo.abc: File already has '.abc' suffix, skipping ``` Note the suffix is shown in **single quotes**. No output file is created (`foo.xz.xz` is NOT produced). (captures: `err_a_hassuffix.*`, `err_a_hassuffix_custom.*`, `err_a_hassuffix_force.*`) ### A.4 Output file exists Compress side (input `c1.txt`, pre-existing `c1.txt.xz`): ``` $ xz c1.txt # exit 1 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: c1.txt.xz: File exists ``` Decompress side (input `d1src.txt.xz`, pre-existing `d1src.txt`): ``` $ xz -d d1src.txt.xz # exit 1 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: d1src.txt: File exists ``` With `-f` both succeed silently: exit 0, empty stderr, existing output is overwritten, input removed as usual. (captures: `err_a_outexists_{compress,compress_f,decompress,decompress_f}.*`) ### A.5 Input is a symlink (to a regular file) ``` $ xz sym.txt # exit 2 $ xz -d sd.txt.xz # exit 2 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: sym.txt: Is a symbolic link, skipping ``` - With `-f`: **follows the symlink and compresses**, exit 0, no message. The output file is named after the symlink (`sym.txt.xz`); the **symlink itself is removed**; the link target (`sym_target.txt`) is left untouched. - With `-c` / `--stdout`: **allowed**, exit 0; compressed data on stdout; neither symlink nor target is removed. - Decompress side behaves the same (`-d` skips with exit 2; `-dc` works, exit 0). (captures: `err_a_symlink_{default,f,c,stdout,d_default,d_c}.*`) ### A.6 Input has more than one hard link ``` $ xz hl2.txt # exit 2 $ xz -d hd2.txt.xz # exit 2 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: hl2.txt: Input file has more than one hard link, skipping ``` - With `-f`: compresses/decompresses normally, exit 0, no message; the named link is removed (other link remains). - With `-c`: allowed, exit 0, no message, nothing removed. (captures: `err_a_hardlink_{default,f,c,d_default,d_f}.*`) ### A.7 Input is not a regular file `/dev/null`, a FIFO (`mkfifo myfifo`), and `/dev/zero` all behave identically when given as named inputs: ``` $ xz /dev/null # exit 2 $ xz -d /dev/null # exit 2 $ xz myfifo # exit 2 $ xz /dev/zero # exit 2 (returns immediately — no read happens) $ xz -f /dev/null # exit 2 — -f does NOT override ``` stderr: ``` PROG: /dev/null: Not a regular file, skipping PROG: myfifo: Not a regular file, skipping PROG: /dev/zero: Not a regular file, skipping ``` - With `-c` the "not a regular file" check is skipped: `xz -c myfifo` and `xz -c /dev/null` succeed (exit 0), treating the input like a stream (`xz -c /dev/null` emits a valid empty .xz stream, 32 bytes). `xz -c /dev/zero | head -c 64` streams zeros fine. (captures: `err_a_devnull_*`, `err_a_fifo_*`, `err_a_devzero_*`) ### A.8 Permission denied (Tested as uid=65534 `nobody` via `setpriv --reuid=nobody --regid=nogroup --clear-groups`, because the session runs as root and root bypasses permission checks.) Unreadable input (mode 000): ``` $ xz perm/noperm.txt # exit 1 $ xz -d perm/noperm2.txt.xz # exit 1 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: perm/noperm.txt: Permission denied PROG: perm/noperm2.txt.xz: Permission denied ``` Unwritable output directory (input readable, dir mode 555): ``` $ xz perm/nowrite/f.txt # exit 1 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: perm/nowrite/f.txt.xz: Permission denied ``` Note the failing name is the **output** path here. (captures: `err_a_perm_denied_*`) ### A.9 Writing to a terminal (pty allocated with `script -qec`) Compressing to a tty stdout is **refused, even with `-f`** (differs from gzip): ``` $ xz < plain.txt # stdout is a tty: exit 1 $ xz -f < plain.txt # exit 1 (same refusal) $ xz -c plain.txt # exit 1 $ xz -cf plain.txt # exit 1 ``` stderr (two lines, `\n`-terminated, verified with `od -c`): ``` PROG: Compressed data cannot be written to a terminal PROG: Try 'PROG --help' for more information. ``` (The second line literally is `Try ' --help' for more information.`) Decompressing to a tty stdout is **allowed** (also differs from gzip): ``` $ xz -dc plain.txt.xz # stdout is a tty: exit 0, decompressed data written $ xz -dcf plain.txt.xz # exit 0 $ xz -d < plain.txt.xz # exit 0 ``` No message at all; plaintext goes to the terminal. (captures: `err_a_tty_*`, exact bytes in `err_a_tty_refusal_stderr.txt`) --- ## SCOPE B — Corruption / format error messages ### B.0 Reference files `ref.xz` = 871 bytes of compressible text (`abcabcabc123\n` × 67, truncated to 871), compressed with defaults (`xz -6`, check = **CRC64** — the default in 5.8.2). Size: 92 bytes. Full hexdump (`od -A d -t x1`): ``` 0000000 fd 37 7a 58 5a 00 00 04 e6 d6 b4 46 04 c0 1c e7 0000016 06 21 01 16 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 76 7d 6c bb 0000032 e0 03 66 00 14 5d 00 30 98 88 a6 1c fb fe 31 f2 0000048 06 3e f8 4f db e1 75 fa 7f f4 00 00 55 ce 78 e2 0000064 6e 77 d7 c5 00 01 38 e7 06 00 00 00 0e 15 e3 94 0000080 b1 c4 67 fb 02 00 00 00 00 04 59 5a ``` Layout of `ref.xz` (offsets decimal): - 0–5 stream magic; 6–7 stream flags (`00 04` = CRC64); 8–11 header CRC32 - 12–31 block header (size byte `04` → 20 bytes; its CRC32 at 28–31) - 32–59 compressed payload (+ 2 padding bytes at 58–59) - 60–67 CRC64 check field; 68–79 index (12 bytes); 80–91 stream footer (footer CRC32 80–83, backward size 84–87 = `02 00 00 00`, magic `59 5A` at 90–91) Other references: `ref-crc32.xz` (88 B), `ref-crc64.xz` (92 B), `ref-sha256.xz` (116 B), `small.xz` = `printf 'a' | xz` (68 B), `empty.xz` = `printf '' | xz` (32 B), `ref.lzma` = `xz -F lzma` of same input (40 B). Sanity: `xz -t ref.xz` → exit 0, both streams empty. `xz -dc ref.xz` → exit 0, 871 bytes on stdout, stderr empty. **General:** for every corruption case below, `xz -t ` and `xz -dc ` print the *same* diagnostic to stderr and exit 1; `-dc` additionally writes whatever partial output was decoded before the failure. Per-file stdout sizes are listed. When decompressing to a *file* (`xz -d bad.xz`), the partial output file is **deleted** on failure and the input `.xz` is kept (verified for payload- and check-corruption cases; exit 1). ### B.1 Truncation (every length) Files truncated to N bytes with `head -c N`, then `xz -t` on the result. (captures: `err_b_trunc32_00..31.*` for `empty.xz`, `err_b_trunc68_00..67.*` for `small.xz`) Result — identical pattern for both files, all exit **1**: | length N | stderr message | |---|---| | 0–5 | `PROG: : File format not recognized` | | 6 … size-1 | `PROG: : Unexpected end of input` | So the only boundary is at 6 bytes (length of the stream magic). A **zero-length file is an error**: `File format not recognized`, exit 1 — also via stdin: `xz -t < /dev/null` and `xz -dc < /dev/null` print `PROG: (stdin): File format not recognized`, exit 1. (`(stdin)` is the literal name used.) Likewise 3 or 6 garbage bytes on stdin give the same message/exit 1. Partial output with `-dc` on truncated files: everything decodable before EOF is written (e.g. `ref.xz` cut at 60 bytes → all 871 payload bytes out, then `Unexpected end of input`, exit 1; `small.xz` cut at 40 → 1 byte out). ### B.2 Stream header corruption (offsets in `ref.xz`) | case | edit | `xz -t` stderr (after `PROG: : `) | exit | `-dc` stdout | |---|---|---|---|---| | magic byte 0 | `b[0]^=0xFF` | `File format not recognized` | 1 | 0 B | | magic byte 5 | `b[5]=0x01` | `File format not recognized` | 1 | 0 B | | flags reserved bits | `b[6]=0xF0`, CRC fixed | `Unsupported options` | 1 | 0 B | | flags reserved high nibble | `b[7]=0x44`, CRC fixed | `Unsupported options` | 1 | 0 B | | header CRC32 | `b[8]^=0xFF` | `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | 0 B | Note: bad magic ⇒ "format not recognized" (decoder falls back to trying .lzma, which also fails); bad reserved flag bits (with *valid* header CRC) ⇒ `Unsupported options`; bad header CRC ⇒ generic `Compressed data is corrupt`. ### B.3 Block header corruption (block header = bytes 12–31) | case | edit | message | exit | `-dc` stdout | |---|---|---|---|---| | size byte = 0 | `b[12]=0x00` | `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | 0 B | | size byte = 0xFF | `b[12]=0xFF` | `Unexpected end of input` | 1 | 0 B | | header body | `b[16]^=0xFF` (filter flags area) | `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | 0 B | | header CRC32 | `b[31]^=0xFF` | `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | 0 B | ### B.4 Payload corruption | case | edit | message | exit | `-dc` stdout | |---|---|---|---|---| | mid-payload | `b[45]^=0xFF` | `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | 17 B partial | | early payload | `b[33]^=0x01` | `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | 615 B partial | Exact text is `Compressed data is corrupt` (not "data error" etc.). The decoder itself detects these (LZMA consistency); output up to the failure point is written. ### B.5 Check-field corruption Check field bytes flipped (CRC32 file: last 2 bytes of its 4-byte check; CRC64 file: byte 62 of ref.xz; SHA-256 file: byte 2 of its 32-byte check): | check type | message | exit | `-dc` stdout | |---|---|---|---| | CRC32 | `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | full 871 B | | CRC64 | `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | full 871 B | | SHA-256 | `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | full 871 B | **The message is the same as payload corruption** — there is no distinct "checksum mismatch" text. `Unexpected end of input` | 1 | 871 B | | `0x05` | `Unsupported type of integrity check; not verifying file integrity`
`Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | 871 B | | `0x0A` (SHA-256, **supported**) | `Compressed data is corrupt` (no warning) | 1 | 871 B | | `0x0F` | `Unsupported type of integrity check; not verifying file integrity`

# 03 — File/Usage Errors and Corruption/Format Errors (xz 5.8.2 at `/workspace/executable`) All captures were made with `LC_ALL=C`. Raw capture files live in `/tmp/xztest/ref/` with prefix `err_`; exit codes are logged in `/tmp/xzprobe_err/exitcodes.log`. **IMPORTANT — program name in messages:** every diagnostic is prefixed with argv[0] verbatim. Since the binary was invoked as `/workspace/executable`, messages begin with `/workspace/executable: `. A clone must print its own argv[0] the same way (`argv[0]: : `). Below, `PROG` denotes that prefix. **Exit-code convention observed (this scope):** - `0` = success - `1` = error (I/O errors, format errors, "File exists", tty refusal, …) - `2` = warning-level "skipping" conditions (directory, suffix, symlink, hardlink, not-a-regular-file). The file is skipped; no output produced. - When both warnings and errors occur in one invocation, the code is `1` (not observed in this scope, but worth checking in multi-file tests). All diagnostics below go to **stderr**; stdout is empty unless stated otherwise. Messages are single lines terminated by `\n` (verified with `od -c`/`sed -n l`; no trailing spaces). --- ## SCOPE A — File/usage error messages ### A.1 Nonexistent input file ``` $ xz nosuchfile.txt # exit 1 $ xz -d nosuchfile.txt.xz # exit 1 ``` stderr (both, with respective filename): ``` PROG: nosuchfile.txt: No such file or directory ``` stdout: empty. (captures: `err_a_nonexist_compress.*`, `err_a_nonexist_decompress.*`) ### A.2 Input is a directory ``` $ xz adir # exit 2 $ xz -d adir # exit 2 $ xz -f adir # exit 2 (same message; -f does NOT override) ``` stderr: ``` PROG: adir: Is a directory, skipping ``` (captures: `err_a_dir_compress.*`, `err_a_dir_decompress.*`, `err_a_dir_compress_f.*`) ### A.3 Input already has the compressor's suffix ``` $ xz foo.xz # exit 2 $ xz -S .abc foo.abc # exit 2 $ xz -f foo.xz # exit 2 — -f does NOT override this check ``` stderr: ``` PROG: foo.xz: File already has '.xz' suffix, skipping PROG: foo.abc: File already has '.abc' suffix, skipping ``` Note the suffix is shown in **single quotes**. No output file is created (`foo.xz.xz` is NOT produced). (captures: `err_a_hassuffix.*`, `err_a_hassuffix_custom.*`, `err_a_hassuffix_force.*`) ### A.4 Output file exists Compress side (input `c1.txt`, pre-existing `c1.txt.xz`): ``` $ xz c1.txt # exit 1 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: c1.txt.xz: File exists ``` Decompress side (input `d1src.txt.xz`, pre-existing `d1src.txt`): ``` $ xz -d d1src.txt.xz # exit 1 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: d1src.txt: File exists ``` With `-f` both succeed silently: exit 0, empty stderr, existing output is overwritten, input removed as usual. (captures: `err_a_outexists_{compress,compress_f,decompress,decompress_f}.*`) ### A.5 Input is a symlink (to a regular file) ``` $ xz sym.txt # exit 2 $ xz -d sd.txt.xz # exit 2 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: sym.txt: Is a symbolic link, skipping ``` - With `-f`: **follows the symlink and compresses**, exit 0, no message. The output file is named after the symlink (`sym.txt.xz`); the **symlink itself is removed**; the link target (`sym_target.txt`) is left untouched. - With `-c` / `--stdout`: **allowed**, exit 0; compressed data on stdout; neither symlink nor target is removed. - Decompress side behaves the same (`-d` skips with exit 2; `-dc` works, exit 0). (captures: `err_a_symlink_{default,f,c,stdout,d_default,d_c}.*`) ### A.6 Input has more than one hard link ``` $ xz hl2.txt # exit 2 $ xz -d hd2.txt.xz # exit 2 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: hl2.txt: Input file has more than one hard link, skipping ``` - With `-f`: compresses/decompresses normally, exit 0, no message; the named link is removed (other link remains). - With `-c`: allowed, exit 0, no message, nothing removed. (captures: `err_a_hardlink_{default,f,c,d_default,d_f}.*`) ### A.7 Input is not a regular file `/dev/null`, a FIFO (`mkfifo myfifo`), and `/dev/zero` all behave identically when given as named inputs: ``` $ xz /dev/null # exit 2 $ xz -d /dev/null # exit 2 $ xz myfifo # exit 2 $ xz /dev/zero # exit 2 (returns immediately — no read happens) $ xz -f /dev/null # exit 2 — -f does NOT override ``` stderr: ``` PROG: /dev/null: Not a regular file, skipping PROG: myfifo: Not a regular file, skipping PROG: /dev/zero: Not a regular file, skipping ``` - With `-c` the "not a regular file" check is skipped: `xz -c myfifo` and `xz -c /dev/null` succeed (exit 0), treating the input like a stream (`xz -c /dev/null` emits a valid empty .xz stream, 32 bytes). `xz -c /dev/zero | head -c 64` streams zeros fine. (captures: `err_a_devnull_*`, `err_a_fifo_*`, `err_a_devzero_*`) ### A.8 Permission denied (Tested as uid=65534 `nobody` via `setpriv --reuid=nobody --regid=nogroup --clear-groups`, because the session runs as root and root bypasses permission checks.) Unreadable input (mode 000): ``` $ xz perm/noperm.txt # exit 1 $ xz -d perm/noperm2.txt.xz # exit 1 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: perm/noperm.txt: Permission denied PROG: perm/noperm2.txt.xz: Permission denied ``` Unwritable output directory (input readable, dir mode 555): ``` $ xz perm/nowrite/f.txt # exit 1 ``` stderr: ``` PROG: perm/nowrite/f.txt.xz: Permission denied ``` Note the failing name is the **output** path here. (captures: `err_a_perm_denied_*`) ### A.9 Writing to a terminal (pty allocated with `script -qec`) Compressing to a tty stdout is **refused, even with `-f`** (differs from gzip): ``` $ xz < plain.txt # stdout is a tty: exit 1 $ xz -f < plain.txt # exit 1 (same refusal) $ xz -c plain.txt # exit 1 $ xz -cf plain.txt # exit 1 ``` stderr (two lines, `\n`-terminated, verified with `od -c`): ``` PROG: Compressed data cannot be written to a terminal PROG: Try 'PROG --help' for more information. ``` (The second line literally is `Try ' --help' for more information.`) Decompressing to a tty stdout is **allowed** (also differs from gzip): ``` $ xz -dc plain.txt.xz # stdout is a tty: exit 0, decompressed data written $ xz -dcf plain.txt.xz # exit 0 $ xz -d < plain.txt.xz # exit 0 ``` No message at all; plaintext goes to the terminal. (captures: `err_a_tty_*`, exact bytes in `err_a_tty_refusal_stderr.txt`) --- ## SCOPE B — Corruption / format error messages ### B.0 Reference files `ref.xz` = 871 bytes of compressible text (`abcabcabc123\n` × 67, truncated to 871), compressed with defaults (`xz -6`, check = **CRC64** — the default in 5.8.2). Size: 92 bytes. Full hexdump (`od -A d -t x1`): ``` 0000000 fd 37 7a 58 5a 00 00 04 e6 d6 b4 46 04 c0 1c e7 0000016 06 21 01 16 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 76 7d 6c bb 0000032 e0 03 66 00 14 5d 00 30 98 88 a6 1c fb fe 31 f2 0000048 06 3e f8 4f db e1 75 fa 7f f4 00 00 55 ce 78 e2 0000064 6e 77 d7 c5 00 01 38 e7 06 00 00 00 0e 15 e3 94 0000080 b1 c4 67 fb 02 00 00 00 00 04 59 5a ``` Layout of `ref.xz` (offsets decimal): - 0–5 stream magic; 6–7 stream flags (`00 04` = CRC64); 8–11 header CRC32 - 12–31 block header (size byte `04` → 20 bytes; its CRC32 at 28–31) - 32–59 compressed payload (+ 2 padding bytes at 58–59) - 60–67 CRC64 check field; 68–79 index (12 bytes); 80–91 stream footer (footer CRC32 80–83, backward size 84–87 = `02 00 00 00`, magic `59 5A` at 90–91) Other references: `ref-crc32.xz` (88 B), `ref-crc64.xz` (92 B), `ref-sha256.xz` (116 B), `small.xz` = `printf 'a' | xz` (68 B), `empty.xz` = `printf '' | xz` (32 B), `ref.lzma` = `xz -F lzma` of same input (40 B). Per-file stdout sizes are listed. When decompressing to a *file* (`xz -d bad.xz`), the partial output file is **deleted** on failure and the input `.xz` is kept (verified for payload- and check-corruption cases; exit 1). ### B.1 Truncation (every length) Files truncated to N bytes with `head -c N`, then `xz -t` on the result. (captures: `err_b_trunc32_00..31.*` for `empty.xz`, `err_b_trunc68_00..67.*` for `small.xz`) Result — identical pattern for both files, all exit **1**: | length N | stderr message | |---|---| | 0–5 | `PROG: : File format not recognized` | | 6 … size-1 | `PROG: : Unexpected end of input` | So the only boundary is at 6 bytes (length of the stream magic). A **zero-length file is an error**: `File format not recognized`, exit 1 — also via stdin: `xz -t < /dev/null` and `xz -dc < /dev/null` print `PROG: (stdin): File format not recognized`, exit 1. `Compressed data is corrupt` | 1 | 871 B | | `0x0A` (SHA-256, **supported**) | `Compressed data is corrupt` (no warning) | 1 | 871 B | | `0x0F` | `Unsupported type of integrity check; not verifying file integrity`
